Deals rotate, so each session starts from an angle and a half the others didn't get. Work from that copy: read whole and as stored, this file pulls every session toward the same shape.

check an output against the dump

how_to_read: 1. Deal first: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/deal.py pomodoro-timer.metadump.json, then read the dealt copy it names for every step below (write-backs go to this file).
2. Read the head: the first 36 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=36, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' pomodoro-timer.metadump.json).
3. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' pomodoro-timer.metadump.json
4. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' pomodoro-timer.metadump.json
5. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' pomodoro-timer.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
6. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' pomodoro-timer.metadump.json returns whole entries.

7. When you have built something that renders, look at it before you finish: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/look.py <your file.html> screenshots it at desktop and phone widths, then plays it (clicks, types, slides, drags and tabs through everything) and lists what breaks along the way and what the page said. Fix what it lists, read its sheet, and look again.

essence.one_sentence: A pomodoro timer is a clock for one indivisible interval: a pause holds the same interval, and the count of finished intervals, not the face, decides what comes next.
essence.summary: Large countdown numerals, one primary control, a clock model that keeps time true (a stored end time or a resynced tick counter), and a finished-interval count that picks the long break.

formula.full: clock model (a deadline timestamp or a tick counter with resync) + finished-interval count + one primary control + large numerals with the phase named

roles.clock model: keeps the remaining time true when the tab is hidden; a deadline timestamp or a tick counter that resyncs against the clock
roles.finished-interval count: picks the long break after four finished intervals
roles.primary control: one press starts, pauses and resumes
roles.numerals: the remaining time, read from across a room
roles.phase name: the state reads without a second look at the number

angles.text: The face is the digits alone on a plain field, with the phase as one word above them, so the time reads from across the room.

angles.angle: ring that fills over the session
angles.text: The digits sit inside a disc whose ring fills as the interval runs, so the share of time gone reads before the numerals do.
A monospaced clock and one status line with no shapes: the phase, the state and the next step are all words.
The face leads with the break that is due next, so each work interval reads as the road to a longer rest.
The count of finished pomodoros is the largest thing on the face, and the clock sits beneath it as the way to the next one.
Each phase fills the whole screen in its own colour, so the phase is seen from the far side of a room before any word is read.

tensions.text: a bare face versus a face that names the state
poles: digits alone, read at a glance
a phase word and colour that say what is running

tensions.text: the cycle moves on its own versus a press at each phase
poles: the next phase starts when the ring ends
the person decides when the break begins

tensions.text: a quiet end versus an end that is heard or seen
poles: a visual end signal in a silent tab
a chime that unlocks on the Start press

llm_brief.text:
On the table: the user's words, quoted: "a timer", "pomodoro", "simple". Sourced values: work 25 minutes; short break 5 (one blog) or 5 to 10; long break 20 to 30 (Wikipedia) or 15 (one blog) after four finished work intervals; WCAG 2.2 pointer targets 24 by 24 CSS px (AA), 44 by 44 (AAA). Clock models, as options: a stored end timestamp read from the clock on each redraw, or a tick counter that resyncs against the clock; either keeps the remaining time honest when the tab is hidden. A pause keeps the remaining time. A count of finished intervals picks the break. Deep cuts: a menubar ring timer with start, pause and reset only, one to 60 minutes, and no outline on the ring; a stepped ring that moves 0.24 degrees a second. Known failures: a bare tick counter with no resync drifting in a hidden tab, a second interval stacked by a repeated Start, a reset that fires while paused. Words in use: Time to focus!, Focus, Break, Long break, Paused.
Ways in: a bare big number with the phase as one word above it; a ring that fills over the session; a quiet text-only status; the long break in view; the count of finished pomodoros as the face; a full-bleed colour per phase. None is marked as the default.
Dials: numeral size 64 to 180 px across phone and desktop; ring band 6 to 20 px; phase colour as three values far apart (a warm red, a green, a dark slate), each with what it signals; progress motion stepped once a second, eased over 300 to 900 ms, or continuous from a start timestamp; end signal as a title change, a finish colour, a vibration, a notification, a flash, or a sound unlocked by the Start press; cycle advance automatic or on a press; reset of the current interval, of the whole cycle, or asking first while running.
Worn paths: the usual move is a count-up stopwatch; fresher: a countdown from 25:00 to 00:00 with the remaining time in view. The usual move is a tomato-shaped kitchen timer; fresher: the technique's own intervals and their names. The usual move is a tick counter with no resync; fresher: a deadline timestamp, or a tick counter that resyncs against the clock. The usual move is a sound at every end; fresher: a visual signal in the tab title, with sound behind a Start press. The usual move is a bare number with no phase named; fresher: the phase named above the digits in a colour and shape of its own. The usual move is a silent reset; fresher: a reset with an undo or a confirm while running.
Open: the platform (default: one self-contained HTML page with inline CSS and JS, opens from disk); the durations (default: 25 work, 5 short break, long break after four, with the 15 to 30 minute spread noted); sound (default: none until the first press).

ak-tt-reset-paused.instead: reset while paused clears the handle and the remaining time, and the state moves to idle
ak-tt-reset-paused.text: Worn path: a reset that leaves a running callback alive after pause.

ak-unprompted-sound.instead: Options once Start is pressed: chime armed by it, title or face flash, notification if permitted, vibration, or silent end.

ak-pomodoro-tomato.excluded_sense: a tomato-shaped kitchen timer as the subject of the task
ak-pomodoro-tomato.instead: the Cirillo time-management technique: work intervals with short and long breaks

ak-timer-stopwatch.excluded_sense: a stopwatch or lap timer that counts up
ak-timer-stopwatch.instead: a countdown from a set interval down to zero

ak-reload-silent.instead: Keep the phase, count and end time in storage, and say on screen what a reload restored.

ak-silent-reset.instead: Reset returns the current session to its start and asks before clearing the day's finished pomodoros, with a one-line undo.

ak-double-start.instead: Start becomes Pause and one timer owns the clock; a second press resumes and does not add an interval.
variants: second interval from a repeated Start press
ak-double-start.text: Worn path: a second Start press creates a second countdown.

ak-tick-drift.instead: Store the end time and read the clock on each redraw; a background tab shows true time on return.
ak-tick-drift.never_implies: A tick counter is fine for the display; it is only wrong as the clock.
ak-tick-drift.text: Worn path: a counter decremented per tick drifts in a background tab.

ak-stopwatch.instead: A countdown from 25:00 to 00:00 with remaining time visible; a log of finished pomodoros.

k-play-end.text: Run a work interval to its end: what does the page say and show?

test.spec: Start is pressed on a 25:00 interval and simulated time reaches 1500 seconds. The numerals read 00:00, the face shows its finish state, the phase label names the short break, and the status line names the next phase. No audio plays before the press.

k-play-reset.text: Start, pause, resume, then reset during a break: does the finished-interval count stay where it was?

test.spec: Start is pressed, Pause at about 10:00 remaining, Resume, the work interval runs to its end, the break starts, then Reset is pressed during the break. The count of finished work intervals reads the same as before the reset, and the break restarts at full length.

k-oracle-break.text: After 1500 seconds of simulated time from Start, which state does the timer show, and how long is its break?

test.spec: 1500 seconds after Start the state is short break with 05:00 remaining.

k-long-break.text: After four finished work intervals, which break comes next, and how long is it?

test.spec: The fourth finished work interval leads to the long break state. Its length falls in the sourced range of 15 to 30 minutes, not the 5-minute short break.

k-pause-resume.text: Pause at 10:00 remaining, wait an hour of simulated time, then resume: what does the numeral show and what is counted?

test.spec: After resume the numeral reads 10:00 and counts down from there. No interval is added to the finished count by the pause.

k-background-tab.text: With the tab hidden for ten simulated minutes, does the numeral match the clock when the tab returns?

test.spec: After 600 seconds hidden, the remaining time shown on return equals the end time minus the clock, within one second.

k-double-start.text: Press Start twice in quick succession: how many interval timers are running afterwards?

test.spec: Exactly one interval timer is active. The second press pauses or resumes the same interval and adds no interval to the count.

k-reload.text: Reload the page in the middle of an interval: what does the face show and say?

test.spec: The face either restores the saved phase and remaining time with a line saying so, or shows idle with a line saying the interval was lost. It does not show a silent reset to 25:00.

k-phone-width.text: At 375 px wide, do the numerals and the primary control fit without horizontal scroll, and is each control at least 24 by 24 CSS px?

test.spec: The document scroll width equals the 375 px viewport. Each control's bounding box is at least 24 px on both sides.

k-greyscale-phase.text: Do the work, short break and long break phases read without colour?

test.spec: In greyscale, the phase name or a shape distinguishes each of the three phases.

k-keyboard.text: With focus on the page body, does Space start and pause the interval, and is Space typed in a text field left alone?

test.spec: Space toggles the primary control with no click. Space typed inside a text input does not toggle the timer.

k-sound-before-press.text: Before the first press, is there any sound, and at session end, what signals it?

test.spec: No audio plays before the first Start press. At session end the signal is visible in the face or the tab title, and sound plays only where audio was unlocked by that press.

k-reset-running.text: Press Reset during a running work interval: does the page ask before clearing it, or offer an undo?

test.spec: Reset during a running interval shows a confirm or an undo, and the interval is still running until that is answered.

q-platform.default: one self-contained HTML page, inline CSS and JS, opens from disk
q-platform.resolve: infer from the prompt; the default is a technical parameter

q-durations.text: Work, short break and long break lengths?
q-durations.default: 25 minutes work, 5 minutes short break, long break after four work intervals; sources spread the long break from 15 to 30 minutes, and the spread is kept
q-durations.resolve: ask the user, or keep the spread

q-sound.text: Does the timer make sound at the end of a session?
q-sound.default: none until the first Start press; a visual end signal as the baseline
q-sound.resolve: ask the user, or infer from the prompt

prompt._about: The user's words, verbatim. The prompt is three words of request: a timer, simple, pomodoro. Their readings are in the lexicon and the map.

pr-timer.text: The user asked for a timer.

pr-pomodoro.text: The timer is a pomodoro timer, as the user named it.

pr-simple.text: The user asked for it to be simple.

pomodoro_cycle._about: Rules of the Pomodoro Technique, from its Wikipedia summary. The creator's own page was not fetched (pomodo.io returned HTTP 429), so the primary source is still open.

pc-interrupt.text: A pomodoro cannot be split: an interruption is either postponed and recorded, or the pomodoro is abandoned.
behaviors: A pause mid-interval is a stop of the same interval, not a second interval
A reset during work counts as an abandoned interval, which the cycle does not count
pc-interrupt.principle: The interval is the unit of attention; interruptions are handled outside it.

pc-ritual.text: The original method leans on physical cues: winding starts the task, ticking keeps it going, and the ring announces the break.
behaviors: A visible start action marks the commitment, not a passive auto-start
The end cue is an announcement, so the end should be heard or seen, not only read from a number
signals: end signal that is not just a digit change

pc-cycle.text: Work in 25-minute intervals with a short break between them; after four intervals, a long break, then the cycle restarts.
properties: the timer rings to end each interval
behaviors: The ring ends the work interval and starts the break
The fourth interval is followed by the longer break, not a short one
The count of finished intervals decides which break comes next

interaction_principles._about: Principles from interaction design, written from general knowledge (inferred). They are not checked against a fetched source.

ix-control.text: Nielsen's heuristic: people need a clear way out of an unwanted state, such as an emergency exit.
behaviors: Reset asks before clearing a running session, or offers undo
Skip for a break is one press and moves to the next phase at once
Phase changes are not hidden behind a timeout the user cannot see
ix-control.principle: The user keeps the cycle in hand; the timer proposes, the person disposes.

ix-fitts.term: Fitts's law and the primary button
ix-fitts.text: Fitts's law: time to hit a target grows with distance and falls with size, so the most-used control should be large and close.
properties: Hick's law: few choices on screen
behaviors: The start/pause control is the largest target on screen
Reset sits apart from the primary control so a stray tap does not clear the cycle
ix-fitts.principle: The primary action is big and near the centre; secondary actions are smaller and further away.

ix-status.text: Nielsen's first heuristic: the interface shows what the system is doing, within a reasonable time.
properties: running or paused shown in words
behaviors: The phase label changes at the moment the phase changes
Paused shows as a state word as well as a frozen number
The count of finished pomodoros stays visible while the timer runs
ix-status.principle: A person glancing from across the desk should know the phase without reading the number twice.

accessibility._about: Accessibility basics for a timer. The target size is sourced from WCAG 2.2; the rest is general knowledge (inferred).

a11y-target.text: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA): pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or have spacing that keeps them apart.
behaviors: Start, pause and reset each clear 24 by 24 CSS px; the primary control clears it well
Undersized controls need enough space that no other control's 24 px circle overlaps them

a11y-announce.text: Phase changes are announced once to assistive tech in a polite live region; the per-second count is not announced.
behaviors: A reader hears the phase change without the count being read every second
A reduced-motion user gets the same ring state as a static colour change
a11y-announce.principle: Announce the event, not the ticking.

faces_and_feedback._about: Rung: timer faces and feedback. Options and examples, not a single face.

rs-face-ring.text: A circle that empties or fills reads as time passing. One builder left the ring's outline off so it does not look like a finish line.
properties: examples in search snippets: FocusRing, Focus
behaviors: A ring with an outline suggests a hard end; without one it grows to a final form on its own
A shrinking ring reads as time left, like a clock face
rs-face-ring.principle: The ring shows elapsed time; an outline makes it look like a finish line.
signals: no outline on the progress track

rs-exemplar-omar.text: A deep-cut personal timer: start, pause and reset only, one to 60 minutes, a ring with no outline.
rs-exemplar-omar.transfers: Dropping the ring outline; timing from the Date object rather than the interval.
rs-exemplar-omar.does_not_transfer: Menu-bar placement (he says it feels detached from the work); a blur background (it looked like a mistake on plain backgrounds).

rs-end-signal.text: Silent end signals seen in the sources: a colour shift near the end, a title change, a visual flash, or a notification that needs permission.
behaviors: A notification needs permission first; a title change needs none
A colour shift in the last seconds only shows if the face is in view
rs-end-signal.principle: Pick a signal that works when the tab is hidden and the sound is off.

rs-sound-notify.term: when sound and notifications may play
rs-sound-notify.text: Notifications and audio both need a user gesture first. Audio that starts from script outside user input is blocked by autoplay rules.
behaviors: Ask for notification permission from a click handler, not on page load
A timer callback starting a sound is not a user gesture; unlock audio at the Start press
rs-sound-notify.principle: The Start press is the one place a sound and a notification are guaranteed to be allowed.

timer_values._about: Rung: the timer's values. Each value is from one named source unless noted.

rs-values-tap.text: WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA) asks pointer targets to be at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels. Text inside a sentence is exempt; a full-sentence link is not.
behaviors: A big start button and small reset button next to each other invites the wrong press (user report)

rs-values-durations.text: Long break after four work sessions: 20 to 30 minutes in Wikipedia, 15 in one blog. Work 25 and short break 5 come from one practitioner's blog, not a primary page.
properties: four work sessions per long break
behaviors: An interrupted pomodoro is indivisible: the interruption is recorded and postponed, or the pomodoro is abandoned (Wikipedia)
rs-values-durations.principle: Values are sourced as single-page facts; do not generalize them to every pomodoro timer.

rs-timing-bugs.text: Common timer bugs: drift from counting ticks, a second interval from a repeated Start press, and a reset that fires while paused. Mostly reasoned, not sourced one by one.
behaviors: A second Start press that creates a second interval runs two countdowns
A callback longer than its interval makes ticks overlap; a recursive setTimeout avoids it (MDN)
A reset button placed where Play was gets pressed by mistake (user report)
rs-timing-bugs.principle: Keep one timer handle and clear it before starting another.

rs-timing-background.text: A tick counter drifts in a background tab; a stored end timestamp does not. Chrome heavily throttles chained timers after five minutes hidden.
behaviors: Interval callbacks can fire later than the delay (MDN)
Remaining time = stored end minus Date.now() stays correct after throttling
A hidden-tab floor near one second was seen in a secondary source (inferred, not on MDN)
rs-timing-background.principle: Compute time from the clock, and let the timer only redraw.

progress_ring._about: Web-found tutorial (DEV repost of a Pomodoro timer build, plain CSS and vanilla JS). What its code does, quoted from the cached page; the article's own prose is marked where it differs from the code.

heading_path: Build a Pomodoro Timer using HTML, CSS and Javascript

sc-tick-model.text: setInterval fires one tick per second; each tick adds one step and moves the red edge by 360 divided by the total seconds.
behaviors: Each tick adds one to progressStart and rewrites the conic-gradient once
The prose calls the divisor minutes; the code divides by progressEnd, which is total seconds
sc-tick-model.principle: Each tick converts a whole-second count to degrees once, so the ring is a function of the tick count.
signals: red arc grows by a fixed step

heading_path: Build a Pomodoro Timer using HTML, CSS and Javascript

sc-ring-face.text: The ring is a conic-gradient background on a 415px disc, with a 400px inner disc carrying the digits.
behaviors: The inner disc covers the gradient, so only a 15px band of the outer disc shows progress
The digits sit on the unchanged dark inner face, separate from the band
sc-ring-face.principle: The face shows the number and the ring shows the share of time gone, in separate layers.
signals: thin coloured band round a dark disc

heading_path: Build a Pomodoro Timer using HTML, CSS and Javascript

sc-end-state.text: On the last tick the whole ring fills green, the interval clears, and the button label returns to START.
behaviors: The finish check is progressStart equal to progressEnd, so the green fill lands on the final tick
The ring jumps from red to green as one change, with no separate done state
sc-end-state.principle: A finished state gets its own colour, so a stopped timer and a finished one read differently.

heading_path: Build a Pomodoro Timer using HTML, CSS and Javascript

sc-state-handling.text: One button toggles on its own label; stop discards progress rather than pausing, and editing the time resets the ring.
behaviors: Stop clears the interval and zeroes progressStart, so the next start runs the full time
Editing minutes or seconds recomputes the total and resets the ring
A zero total shows an alert instead of starting
sc-state-handling.principle: Stop here is a reset, so a resume needs state the article does not keep; the article names PAUSE as the missing piece.
signals: START and STOP swap on click

sc-drift-risk.term: drift risk of a tick count
sc-drift-risk.text: Counting interval ticks instead of reading a clock lets the displayed time fall behind real time when ticks run late.
behaviors: Each interval call adds one second of progress whatever the wall clock says
A delayed or throttled timer finishes after the set time has really passed
A start timestamp compared with the current time would stay accurate across delays
sc-drift-risk.principle: Derive remaining time from a start timestamp, not from how many ticks have fired.
signals: timer ends after the real set time
sc-drift-risk.note: Inferred from the tick code, not stated by the page. A Chrome throttling article is in the cache under key 5b6447bc8092db82 for a research ticket to cite.

face._about: Visual face of a single-purpose pomodoro timer, as one web timer shows it. Describes what transfers, not the brand.

scr-face-rest.text: At rest one large centred clock reads 25:00 on a solid phase colour, with a single full-width START button and a round counter above the status line.
behaviors: The biggest element is the remaining time, so it reads at a glance from across a room
Phase tabs Pomodoro, Short Break and Long Break sit above the clock and show the active phase by a filled pill
The task list sits below the timer and does not compete with it
scr-face-rest.principle: One number and one action dominate; everything else is labelled and quiet.
signals: phase shown by colour and pill

scr-face-running.text: The page offers a dark face for the running state and a compact small-window mode, but its text does not describe the countdown visuals themselves.
behaviors: Turning the face dark while running cuts glare during long focus blocks
A small window keeps the clock visible beside other work
scr-face-running.principle: The running state can change the surroundings without changing the number.

scr-controls.text: Controls are one START/PAUSE button, phase switches, and keyboard shortcuts; automatic start of breaks and of pomodoros is a setting.
behaviors: Space starts or pauses from anywhere, so the timer needs no mouse
Keys 1, 2 and 3 jump straight to Pomodoro, Short Break or Long Break
Auto start is off by default in the settings list, so the user chooses whether a break starts itself
scr-controls.principle: The primary action has a key; secondary actions sit behind a settings panel.

scr-end-state.text: The end of a round is signalled by an alarm, optionally also on a phone with the screen off; the user starts the break by hand unless auto start is on.
properties: alarm type Pomodoro Breaks Both None
behaviors: Alarm type Breaks fires only when a break ends, so a user who wants only the break cue hears one sound
A phone alarm runs even when the screen is off, which covers a timer left running on a desk
When every task is done the task area says so instead of showing an empty list
scr-end-state.principle: The end of a round is an event the user has to hear or see; which rounds ring is their choice.

heading_path: How to Use the Mobile Alarm Feature

phone_layout._about: Phone timer layout as captioned in the ScreensDesign gallery. Captions only; screen images did not load in the fetch.

options._about: options, not requirements: phone arrangements beyond the captioned gallery screen. Inferred layouts, not sourced.

opt-phone-top-number.term: top number, controls in a thumb row
opt-phone-top-number.text: The countdown sits high on the screen and the controls run along a row near the bottom edge, within thumb reach.
properties: start, pause and reset in one row
behaviors: The numerals read first at the top, and the thumb reaches the row without stretching across the screen
On a tall phone the number and the row sit far apart, so the eye travels between them
signals: controls in a row near the bottom edge

opt-phone-presets.term: number with a row of presets
opt-phone-presets.text: The countdown sits centred, with a row of three preset durations under it and one start control.
behaviors: A preset changes the duration in one tap, so the most-used lengths need no settings screen
Three presets keep the row short; a fourth duration needs a settings route
signals: three small buttons beneath the digits

sc-phone-layout.text: Phone timer screen: a centred countdown, one central play or pause button, and a bottom navigation bar of three icons, with edit and reset icons at the top.
behaviors: The central play button becomes a pause button while a countdown runs
Edit and reset sit in the top corner, away from the central control
signals: countdown with pause in the middle

timer_face._about: The large countdown face, from captions. Typeface, size and colour are not in the captions.

sc-timer-face.text: A large digital mm:ss countdown on a plain field, the timer as the dominant element of the screen.
behaviors: The countdown shows minutes and seconds mid-session, such as 24:49 or 00:57
signals: digital time with no clock face

modes._about: Work and break intervals as configured in the app, from captions.

sc-modes.term: work, short break and long break modes
sc-modes.text: Three interval kinds: a flow (work) of 25:00, a short break of 05:00, and a long break of 30:00, with the flow and break durations and a cycle of flows set in settings.
behaviors: The flow and break durations are set on a Pomodoro timer settings screen
A cycle selection modal lets the user select flows, shown with four selected

timing_rules._about: Cycle, states, clock and the oracle values a test can check. The technique's numbers are sourced; the state machine and clock model are derived (inferred).

options._about: options, not requirements: clock and reset decision points, cycle advance. Builder choices where the sources are silent.

opt-clock-model.text: Stored end timestamp (survives throttling; needs pause bookkeeping) or a tick counter decremented each second (simplest; drifts when the tab is hidden).

opt-reset-scope.text: Reset the current interval and keep the finished count; reset the whole cycle to the first work interval; or reset the interval and ask first when it is running.

opt-advance.text: Break and next work interval start on their own when the ring ends, or wait for a press after the ring. The original method treats the ring as the break signal.

tr-states.text: Five states: idle, running a work interval, paused, short break, long break. Each transition is one press or one zero-crossing.
behaviors: idle to running work: one Start press; the page does not start by itself on load
running work to short or long break: the remaining time reaches zero; a break starts
running work to paused: a Pause press keeps the remaining time
paused to running work: Start resumes from the stored remaining time, not from full length
break to running work: the break ends, by a press or by the auto setting
any state to idle: reset, scope set by the options below
tr-states.principle: Phase and pause are separate facts: a paused work interval is still a work interval.
signals: phase label changes at the moment of the switch

tr-pause.text: Pause stops the same interval. Resume continues it from the stored remaining time, and the paused time does not count as a new interval.
behaviors: A pause at 10:00 remaining and a resume an hour later shows 10:00 and counts down from there
Pausing does not add a finished interval to the count
tr-pause.principle: Pausing is a stop of the same unit, not the start of a new one.

tr-cycle.text: Work intervals of 25 minutes, short breaks between them, and a long break after four work intervals, then the cycle starts again.
properties: four work intervals before the long break
behaviors: The fourth completed work interval leads to the long break, not a short one
Only completed work intervals advance the count toward the long break
tr-cycle.principle: The long break is a counted event: the count of finished intervals picks its length.

tr-oracle.text: Checkable values: a work interval started at 00:00 reaches a break at 25:00 of elapsed time, and the fourth finished interval leads to a long break.
behaviors: Simulated time of 1500 seconds after Start gives the break state, with break length 5 minutes
Simulated time of 1500 seconds after the fourth finished interval gives a long break: 15 minutes in one blog, 20 to 30 in Wikipedia
Pause at 600 seconds remaining, any elapsed time, resume: still 600 seconds remaining

tr-clock.text: Two clock models keep the time honest: a deadline read from the clock, or a tick counter that resyncs against the clock.
behaviors: Deadline: store the end time and show end minus now on each redraw; a throttled tick does not lose time, but a pause stores the remaining time
Tick counter with resync: decrement a seconds value on each tick and read the clock to correct it; simplest to build, and it recovers after throttling
A bare tick counter loses time while the tab is hidden until a resync corrects it
Chrome checks chained timers in a hidden tab about once a minute after five minutes hidden
tr-clock.principle: Both models keep the clock as the reference; they differ in whether the time is computed or corrected.

face_and_feedback._about: Readings, options and spreads for the face, the progress motion, the end-of-session signal and the finished-timer checks. Options side by side, not one face.

options._about: options, not requirements: how a phase and an end are signalled. Builder choices where the sources are silent.

opt-phase-mapping.text: Choose how each phase is carried: a colour family per phase, a phase word above the digits, or a filled tab. Each reads differently at a distance.
behaviors: Colour per phase reads from across a room but fails in greyscale unless a word or shape also differs
A phase word works in greyscale and for colour-blind users, but is read more slowly at a glance
A filled tab shows all three phases at once, so the next phase is visible before it starts

opt-end-signal-mapping.text: Choose which signal marks each end: a title change, a notification where permission was given, a sound unlocked by the Start press, a vibration on phones, or a finish colour on the face.
behaviors: A title change shows in the tab strip with the tab hidden and needs no permission
A notification needs permission asked from a click, and it can fire later with the tab hidden
A sound plays only where the Start press unlocked audio; a timer callback cannot start it alone
Pairing two signals covers a case one alone misses, such as a muted sound with the tab hidden

fb-finish-checks.text: A finished timer can be checked at phone and desktop widths: the digits read 00:00, the face shows its finish state, and the start control has come back.
properties: status line names the next phase
behaviors: At 375 px the numerals and the one button fit with no horizontal scroll
At 1280 px the same face keeps the numerals centred in the card
fb-finish-checks.principle: The finished state is checked by the numerals, the colour and the control together.

test.spec: text of the numeral element matches ^00:00$

signals.text: No horizontal scroll at phone width

test.spec: document scrollWidth equals the viewport width at 375 px

signals.text: Primary button label is back to START or the next start label

test.spec: button text is START or the next phase's start label

fb-phases.text: Each phase can be carried by a colour family, a label, a filled tab or the ring colour. The colour families below are far apart, not a palette to adopt.
behaviors: A full-bleed colour per phase tells the phase from across a room
A label-only difference keeps one face colour, so the words carry the phase
fb-phases.principle: Colour, words and shape each carry the phase on their own; combining them is one option among several.

test.spec: the phase name or a shape distinguishes each phase in greyscale

fb-simple-face.text: Simple counts what sits on the face; each reading sets that count differently.

readings.in_practice: Digits and one START/PAUSE control, the phase name as a word.
signals: one number and one button on screen while running

readings.reading: one screen with a few plain controls
readings.in_practice: Digits, phase row, reset and settings link, text-labelled, undecorated.
signals: controls have text labels, no gradients or shadows

readings.reading: a quiet face with one accent colour
readings.in_practice: Neutral ground, grey digits, one accent for the phase or the primary button.
signals: one saturated colour on the face

readings.reading: a face that is only text
readings.in_practice: Monospaced digits and a status line, no drawn shapes.
signals: no svg, canvas, ring, bar or icon

fb-progress-motion.text: A progress ring or bar can move three ways: stepped once a second, eased per tick, or linear and continuous. Each is a reading.
behaviors: A stepped ring moves in fixed angles, so a 25 minute ring moves 0.24 degrees a second
An eased transition of 300 to 900 ms makes each step look continuous, and the ring lags the numerals by that transition
A continuous sweep recomputed from a start timestamp stays correct after a throttled background tab
fb-progress-motion.principle: Stepped motion matches the once-a-second numerals; continuous motion needs a timestamp to stay accurate.

fb-progress-checks.text: A 25 minute ring can be checked against its angle at a fixed time. Reduced motion can drop the eased step and keep the stepped ring.

signals.text: Ring angle after 60 seconds of a 25 minute session

test.spec: ring angle is 14.4 degrees at 60 s of 1500 s, within 0.5 degree

fb-end-signal.text: The end of a session can be signalled by a title change, a finish colour on the face, a vibration, a notification, a flash, or a sound. Each misses some case.
behaviors: A title change shows in the tab strip while the tab is in the background
A finish colour (red to green in one tick, as the sourced tutorial does) reads differently from a stopped face
A flash on the face is seen only while the tab is in view
fb-end-signal.principle: Each signal misses a case (hidden tab, muted sound, no permission), so pairing two covers more than one alone.

signals.text: The title changes at session end with the tab hidden

test.spec: with the tab in the background, the document title or the favicon changes at session end

fb-end-signal-rules.term: permission and autoplay rules for end signals
fb-end-signal-rules.text: The browser gates sound and notifications: a title change needs no permission, a notification needs one, and sound needs a user gesture.
behaviors: A notification needs permission, and the request works from a click handler, not from page load
A sound plays when audio was unlocked by the Start press; a timer callback starting audio is not a user gesture
A title change needs no permission and works with the tab hidden
fb-end-signal-rules.principle: Asking for audio and notification permission on the first press lets the end signal fire later from a timer.

fb-face-number.text: The countdown can be digits alone, digits in a ring, over a bar, or under words. Digits alone is the plainest reading of simple.
behaviors: Legible digits-only: high contrast on a plain field, tabular figures so the width does not shift
Pushed further: numerals filling the viewport edge to edge, in one very heavy or very light weight
A ring behind the numerals shows time gone while the digits stay put
fb-face-number.principle: The number is what gets read at a glance; a ring or bar adds a second channel without moving it.

signals.text: Numerals are the largest element on the face

test.spec: numeral height is at least 3 times the button label height at 375 px and at 1280 px

tokens.ring_band_px: 6 to 20 (sourced band: 15 px on a 415 px disc)

controls_and_access._about: Controls, keys, announcements, phone layout, persistence and the count. Required core and optional extras are separate; persistence and skip are options, not requirements.

options._about: options, not requirements: decision points where nothing sourced decides it

opt-persist-none.text: Each load starts at idle with a count of zero. A reload loses the interval and the count.

opt-persist-session.text: Survives a reload in the same tab; a closed tab starts over. Wrap reads and writes in try/catch, since some private windows throw.

opt-persist-local.text: A count and a stored end time survive across days. Tradeoffs: a stale interval after a long gap, a log that grows, and storage that can be blocked. Store the end time, not a tick counter.

opt-reset-cycle.text: A second reset scope that rewinds to the first interval and clears the count, shown as a separate, confirmed action.

opt-skip.text: Skip a break in one press, moving to the next work interval. Skip a session as an option that does not add to the count.

opt-keys-reset.text: R to reset and S to skip a break, each with a confirm or undo so a stray key does not clear a running interval.

cc-control-set.text: Start, pause, resume and reset cover the job; skip and auto-start are optional extras.
properties: pause and resume as one toggle
behaviors: Start, pause and resume share one control, so the face has one primary action
Reset sits apart from the toggle, so a stray tap does not clear the interval
Auto-start is a setting, so the cycle can run with no setup
cc-control-set.principle: The core set is what the job needs; extras stay one step away.

cc-keyboard.text: A reference timer maps the space bar to start and pause from anywhere on the page.
behaviors: Space toggles the primary control, the same as a click on it
Key presses stay out of text fields, so typing a label does not toggle the timer

cc-announce.text: A phase change is announced once; focus stays on the control that was pressed.
properties: reduced motion keeps the same ring state
behaviors: A screen reader hears the new phase once, not the countdown each second
Moving focus into the new phase on its own would pull it away from whatever the person is doing
cc-announce.principle: Announce the event, not the ticking.

cc-phone.term: phone tap targets and control placement
cc-phone.text: WCAG 2.2 AA sets a 24 by 24 CSS px floor for pointer targets; SC 2.5.5 (AAA) sets 44 by 44.
properties: reset in a corner, apart from the toggle
behaviors: A large centred toggle clears both sizes with room to spare
Reset in a corner keeps a thumb's stray tap away from the toggle

cc-bind-reset.text: Reset returns the current interval to its full length. Whether it also rewinds the cycle is a decision point.
properties: current interval back to full length
a confirm or undo before a running interval is cleared
behaviors: Reset during a break restarts that break and leaves the count where it is
A reset during work is an abandoned interval, which the cycle does not count

cc-count.text: The count of finished work intervals decides which break comes next.
properties: fourth interval triggers the long break
behaviors: The count rises when a work interval reaches its end, not when it starts
A paused interval adds nothing until it ends

cc-words.text: A reference timer's status line at rest reads 'Time to focus!'; the other state words are readings to choose from.
behaviors: Paused is a state word beside the frozen number
Break names the phase the ring has just moved into
never_implies: 'Done' does not mean the day is finished
'Reset' does not mean the count is erased

domain_vocabulary._about: Vocabulary and associations for a pomodoro timer. Keyword registers, associations with deep cuts, influences, the quality readings of 'simple', and search phrases. Seed material, not requirements.

sq-focus.text: Phrases people type when they want a focus countdown.

sq-face.text: Phrases people type when they want a particular look.

lx-technique-words.text: Cirillo vocabulary, from the technique's own summary: the unit is the interval, and interruptions are handled outside it.

lx-technical.text: Words for how time is kept, how the phase changes, and how the change is announced.

lx-perceptual-mood.text: How the face looks and feels: the number from across a desk, a plain ground, and a calm tone that tightens near the end.

lx-objects.text: The parts a pomodoro timer is made of.

lx-associations.text: How people talk about the timer, including the less obvious links.
behaviors: Parkinson's law: work stretches to fill the time, so a countdown works as a boundary
Zeigarnik effect: an unfinished interval stays in mind, which is why the end cue matters
Ultradian rhythm: attention rises and falls in waves, so 25 minutes is a fraction of one wave
contribution: tomato: the shape of the original timer, a nod rather than the subject
bell: the end as a sound the page can echo visually
hourglass: time as something that runs out, not a clock face

lx-influences.text: Lineages that shape the timer, each with what it brings.
contribution: the Pomodoro Technique (Cirillo): the 25 and 5 interval, the long break after four, the indivisible interval
kitchen timer: one dial, one ring, one job
focus and flow writing: attention as the unit, interruptions handled outside the interval
Cirillo's own book: the to-do list and activity record kept beside the timer

lx-quality-simple.text: A size word for how much setup the person does. The surface readings are in fb-simple-face.

readings.reading: behaviour: the cycle runs with no setup
readings.in_practice: Work, short and long break run in order with preset durations; one press starts the cycle.
signals: no settings screen needed to start

readings.reading: behaviour: one press starts each phase
readings.in_practice: Each phase waits for a press, so the person decides when a break starts.

readings.reading: behaviour: the rules show as one short line
readings.in_practice: One plain line, e.g. 'Work 25, break 5, long break after four'.
